findings.text: `bytes.toString('utf8')` keeps a UTF-8 byte-order mark (U+FEFF), unlike a standard UTF-8 decode (TextDecoder strips it). countLines only treats ' ' and '\t' as whitespace before a special character, so in a file with a BOM a first line like `﻿// header` or `﻿/* … */` is counted as code instead of a comment. A BOM'd shebang (`﻿#!…`) also misses the shebang rule, so in a `#`-comment language it is counted as a comment instead of code. The fix is to strip a leading BOM, or decode with `new TextDecoder()`.

Each file is read whole (`readFile`) before the 8,000-byte binary check. This wastes memory on large binaries. A binary file over 2 GiB (disk image, archive) makes readFile throw ERR_FS_FILE_TOO_LARGE, which aborts the whole scan (the CLI exits 1) when the goal says such a file should be left out. Reading only the first 8,000 bytes before deciding would fix it.

Any readdir or readFile error has no handling. One unreadable subfolder or file (EACCES), or a file removed between readdir and readFile (ENOENT), aborts the whole report: cli.ts prints `loc: …` and exits 1, so the user gets no output at all instead of a report of everything else.

`stat(folder).catch(() => null)` treats every stat failure as missing. A folder that exists but can't be stat'ed (EACCES on a parent, ELOOP, ENAMETOOLONG) is reported as `no such folder`, which is wrong. The exit code 2 is still right.

'reads UTF-8 text' does not test UTF-8 decoding. The non-ASCII characters are in a comment and in a string, and decoding the bytes as latin1 (or anything else) gives the same counts, so a wrong decoding would still pass. A real check needs content whose counts depend on the decoding, for example a BOM before a comment, or a check of the decoded text.

No test covers the entry point the goal names (`node dist/cli.js`). The tests drive `run` from report.ts with an injected cwd. Nothing checks that cli.ts passes process.cwd() for the default folder, sets the process exit code (0/2), or that the build emits a runnable dist/cli.js. The catch path's exit code 1 is also untested.

blind.summary: I found no blockers. The goal is met as specified: scanFolder, summarize and the command (table and --json output, exit code 2 with a `loc: ` message on stderr) all behave as the goal asks, and the main tests check real values. I did not run the tests or the build because this review was read-only, so all findings come from reading the code. What's left is a set of minor defects. A UTF-8 byte-order mark changes how the first line is counted. Every file is read in full just to check whether it's binary, so a binary file over 2 GiB crashes the scan. One unreadable or vanished file or folder aborts the whole report with exit code 1. A stat failure other than "not found" is reported as "no such folder". The UTF-8 test would pass under any decoding, and nothing tests cli.ts itself.
